rebuttals.argument: The Challenger's caution is reasonable design guidance but does not describe a defect in the current artifact. Two things are worth separating: first, no code exists yet, so there is nothing to check for a hardcoded-vs-computed value; this is a plan describing a schema, not an implementation. Second, the literal string quoted, 'C-008 as amended in constitution version 2,' most plausibly denotes the constitution version in which the retirement clause was introduced into C-008's text, i.e. a historical amendment marker, not a claim about the constitution version current at retirement time. Read that way, a fixed string is actually correct and stable, since the amendment date/version of C-008 doesn't change every time an unrelated constraint (like this C-004 phrasing history shows) gets revised. That said, the Challenger's underlying worry, that a future implementation must not silently go stale relative to load_governing_constitution(), is legitimate and worth carrying forward as an implementation note. I'd recommend the eventual ledger/retire.py derive the 'amended in version N' figure from the constitution's own amendment history rather than typing a literal, but flag this as a refinement for the code-writing step, not a flaw in the plan under review.
